grade.rationale: The candidate exactly matches the reference: the change event (supported limit raised from 8 to 16 in v1.1) and the current truth (Atlas Runner 1.1 supports 16 concurrent jobs) are both stated and cited to atlas-release-2, and the v1.0/8-job fact is preserved as historical with explicit supersession, cited to atlas-release-1. Versions 1.0 and 1.1 are kept distinct, so no false merge; the 8-job limit is framed as superseded history rather than current, so no stale-current leak; and the historical claim is retained, so no lost history. Every factual claim is grounded in the two primary snapshots, including the accurate meta-claims about what the sources do and do not cover, hence zero unsupported claims. The sole weakness is the unresolved section: the reference lists nothing unresolved, and two of the three items (hard cap vs. configurable; editions/tiers/deployment modes) are invented peripheral questions that earn no credit; the post-1.1 corpus-boundary note is a defensible hedge, yielding partial credit. The answer is otherwise well-structured, fully cited, and decision-useful.
